import os
from collections.abc import Iterator

from sqlmodel import Session, SQLModel, create_engine

DATABASE_URL = os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL", "sqlite:///./inventory.db")
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False} if DATABASE_URL.startswith("sqlite") else {})


def init_db() -> None:
    SQLModel.metadata.create_all(engine)


def get_session() -> Iterator[Session]:
    with Session(engine) as session:
        yield session
from sqlmodel import Field, SQLModel


class ItemBase(SQLModel):
    name: str
    price_cents: int


class Item(ItemBase, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)


class ItemCreate(ItemBase):
    pass


class ItemRead(ItemBase):
    id: int
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from sqlmodel import Session

from app.db import get_session, init_db
from app.models import Item, ItemCreate, ItemRead


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    init_db()
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
SessionDep = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]


@app.post("/items", response_model=ItemRead)
def create_item(item: ItemCreate, session: SessionDep) -> Item:
    db_item = Item.model_validate(item)
    session.add(db_item)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_item)
    return db_item
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import app


def test_create_item():
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        r = client.post("/items", json={"name": "pen", "price_cents": 150})
        assert r.status_code == 200
        assert r.json()["name"] == "pen"

content.text: ### Get a List of Relationship Objects Source: https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/blob/main/docs/tutorial/relationship-attributes/read-relationships.md Accesses the heroes relationship attribute on a team object to get a list of all related heroes. ```python def select_heroes(): with Session(engine) as session: statement = select(Team).where(Team.name == "Preventers") result = session.exec(statement) team_preventers = result.one() print("Preventers heroes:", team_preventers.heroes) ``` -------------------------------- ### Read Relationships > Get a List of Relationship Objects Source: https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/blob/main/docs/tutorial/relationship-attributes/read-relationships.md And the same way, when we are working on the **many** side of the **one-to-many** relationship, we can get a list of the related objects just by accessing the relationship attribute: -------------------------------- ### Select Heroes with Join in SQLModel Source: https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/blob/main/docs/tutorial/connect/read-connected-data.md Use select(Hero, Team).join(Team) to join tables in SQLModel. The ON condition is inferred from the foreign_key in the model definition. Include Team in the select to access its data. ```python def select_heroes(): with Session(engine) as session: statement = select(Hero, Team).join(Team) results = session.exec(statement) for hero, team in results: print("Hero:", hero, "Team:", team) ``` -------------------------------- ### The Value of `back_populates` Source: https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/blob/main/docs/tutorial/relationship-attributes/back-populates.md ## The Value of `back_populates` Now that you know why `back_populates` is there, let's review the exact value again. It's quite simple code, it's just a string, but it might be confusing to think exactly *what* string should go there: ```python from sqlmodel import Field, Relationship, Session, SQLModel, create_engine, select class Team(SQLModel, table=True): id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True) name: str = Field(index=True) headquarters: str heroes: list["Hero"] = Relationship(back_populates="team") class Hero(SQLModel, table=True): id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True) name: str = Field(index=True) secret_name: str age: int | None = Field(default=None, index=True) team_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="team.id") team: Team | None = Relationship(back_populates="heroes") ``` The string in `back_populates` is the name of the attribute *in the other* model, that will reference *the current* model. So, in the class `Team`, we have an attribute `heroes` and we declare it with `Relationship(back_populates="team")`. ```python class Team(SQLModel, table=True): id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True) name: str = Field(index=True) headquarters: str heroes: list["Hero"] = Relationship(back_populates="team") ``` The string in `back_populates="team"` refers to the attribute `team` in the class `Hero` (the other class). And, in the class `Hero`, we declare an attribute `team`, and we declare it with `Relationship(back_populates="heroes")`. So, the string `"heroes"` refers to the attribute `heroes` in the class `Team`. ```python class Hero(SQLModel, table=True): id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True) name: str = Field(index=True) secret_name: str age: int | None = Field(default=None, index=True) team_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="team.id") team: Team | None = Relationship(back_populates="heroes") ``` /// tip Each **relationship attribute** points to the other one, in the other model, using `back_populates`. /// Although it's simple code, it can be confusing to think about 😵, because the same line has concepts related to both models in multiple places: * Just by being in the **current** model, the line has something to do with the current model. * The name of the attribute is about the **other** model. * The type annotation is about the **other** model. * And the `back_populates` refers to an attribute in the **other** model, that points to the **current** model. -------------------------------- ### Hero model with back_populates Source: https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/blob/main/docs/tutorial/relationship-attributes/back-populates.md Shows the Hero model with the team relationship attribute using back_populates="heroes", which refers to the heroes attribute in the Team model. ```python class Hero(SQLModel, table=True): id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True) name: str = Field(index=True) secret_name: str age: int | None = Field(default=None, index=True) team_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="team.id") team: Team | None = Relationship(back_populates="heroes") ```

class Order(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    customer_email: str = Field(index=True)

    lines: list["OrderLine"] = Relationship(back_populates="order")


class OrderLine(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    order_id: int = Field(foreign_key="order.id", index=True)
    item_id: int = Field(foreign_key="item.id")
    quantity: int
    # Price snapshot at order time so totals don't change if the item price does.
    unit_price_cents: int

    order: Order | None = Relationship(back_populates="lines")


class OrderLineCreate(SQLModel):
    item_id: int
    quantity: int = Field(gt=0)


class OrderCreate(SQLModel):
    customer_email: str = Field(pattern=r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$")
    lines: list[OrderLineCreate] = Field(min_length=1)


class OrderLineRead(SQLModel):
    item_id: int
    quantity: int
    unit_price_cents: int


class OrderRead(SQLModel):
    id: int
    customer_email: str
    lines: list[OrderLineRead]
    total_cents: int
EOF

p='app/main.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI\nfrom sqlmodel import Session","from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException\nfrom sqlmodel import Session")
s=s.replace("from app.models import Item, ItemCreate, ItemRead","from app.models import (\n    Item,\n    ItemCreate,\n    ItemRead,\n    Order,\n    OrderCreate,\n    OrderLine,\n    OrderRead,\n)")
s+='''

def to_order_read(order: Order) -> OrderRead:
    return OrderRead(
        id=order.id,
        customer_email=order.customer_email,
        lines=[
            {"item_id": l.item_id, "quantity": l.quantity, "unit_price_cents": l.unit_price_cents}
            for l in order.lines
        ],
        total_cents=sum(l.quantity * l.unit_price_cents for l in order.lines),
    )


@app.post("/orders", response_model=OrderRead)
def create_order(data: OrderCreate, session: SessionDep) -> OrderRead:
    order = Order(customer_email=data.customer_email)
    for line in data.lines:
        item = session.get(Item, line.item_id)
        if item is None:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {line.item_id} not found")
        order.lines.append(
            OrderLine(item_id=item.id, quantity=line.quantity, unit_price_cents=item.price_cents)
        )
    session.add(order)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(order)
    return to_order_read(order)


@app.get("/orders/{order_id}", response_model=OrderRead)
def get_order(order_id: int, session: SessionDep) -> OrderRead:
    order = session.get(Order, order_id)
    if order is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Order not found")
    return to_order_read(order)

def make_item(client, name, price):
    return client.post("/items", json={"name": name, "price_cents": price}).json()["id"]


def test_create_order_total(client):
    pen = make_item(client, "pen", 150)
    pad = make_item(client, "pad", 400)
    r = client.post(
        "/orders",
        json={
            "customer_email": "a@example.com",
            "lines": [{"item_id": pen, "quantity": 3}, {"item_id": pad, "quantity": 1}],
        },
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["total_cents"] == 850
    assert body["customer_email"] == "a@example.com"
    assert len(body["lines"]) == 2


def test_get_order(client):
    pen = make_item(client, "pen", 150)
    oid = client.post(
        "/orders",
        json={"customer_email": "a@example.com", "lines": [{"item_id": pen, "quantity": 2}]},
    ).json()["id"]
    r = client.get(f"/orders/{oid}")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json()["total_cents"] == 300
    assert client.get("/orders/999").status_code == 404


def test_unknown_item_404(client):
    r = client.post(
        "/orders",
        json={"customer_email": "a@example.com", "lines": [{"item_id": 42, "quantity": 1}]},
    )
    assert r.status_code == 404


def test_validation(client):
    pen = make_item(client, "pen", 150)
    line = {"item_id": pen, "quantity": 1}
    assert client.post("/orders", json={"customer_email": "a@example.com", "lines": []}).status_code == 422
    assert client.post("/orders", json={"customer_email": "bad", "lines": [line]}).status_code == 422
    zero = {"item_id": pen, "quantity": 0}
    assert client.post("/orders", json={"customer_email": "a@example.com", "lines": [zero]}).status_code == 422
EOF

from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from sqlmodel import Session

from app.db import get_session, init_db
from app.models import Item, ItemCreate, ItemRead


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    init_db()
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
SessionDep = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]


@app.post("/items", response_model=ItemRead)
def create_item(item: ItemCreate, session: SessionDep) -> Item:
    db_item = Item.model_validate(item)
    session.add(db_item)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_item)
    return db_item

def to_order_read(order: Order) -> OrderRead:

        customer_email=order.customer_email,
        lines=[
            {"item_id": l.item_id, "quantity": l.quantity, "unit_price_cents": l.unit_price_cents}
            for l in order.lines
        ],
        total_cents=sum(l.quantity * l.unit_price_cents for l in order.lines),

@app.post("/orders", response_model=OrderRead)
def create_order(data: OrderCreate, session: SessionDep) -> OrderRead:
    order = Order(customer_email=data.customer_email)
    for line in data.lines:
        item = session.get(Item, line.item_id)
        if item is None:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {line.item_id} not found")
        order.lines.append(
            OrderLine(item_id=item.id, quantity=line.quantity, unit_price_cents=item.price_cents)
        )
    session.add(order)

    session.refresh(order)

    order = session.get(Order, order_id)

def make_item(client, name, price):
